brief.subject: FBI flags midterm election scams; sextortion fixer halted
brief.headline: FBI Warns of Midterm Election Scams as FTC Halts a Sextortion Relief Scheme
brief.dek: Fraudsters target the 2026 midterms, a court freezes a sextortion fixer, and Walmart wire-fraud victims get more than $9.8 million back.
brief.lede: The FBI says scammers are using the 2026 U.S. midterm election to run multiple fraud schemes. Expect more election-themed pitches as November nears.

sections.heading: Midterm election scams are rising
bullets: On Oct. 15, the FBI warned that scammers are exploiting the 2026 midterm election for multiple fraud schemes.
A separate FBI alert cautions voters about election crimes ahead of the November 2026 vote.
Treat unexpected election-themed calls, texts or donation requests with suspicion until you verify them on your own.

sections.heading: Sextortion rescue service frozen by court
bullets: A federal court temporarily halted Digital Forensics Corporation LLC and its CEO at the FTC's request.
The FTC alleges the firm took millions of dollars by falsely promising to identify sextortion criminals and stop attacks.
Sextortion victims can be hit twice, so be wary of paid services claiming they can make the threats end.

sections.heading: Walmart wire-fraud victims get refunds
bullets: The FTC is sending payments totaling more than $9.8 million to people scammed through Walmart's wire transfer services.
The agency alleged Walmart failed to stop scammers who took hundreds of millions of dollars from U.S. consumers.
Walmart settled the charges in June 2025, including claims it lacked effective anti-fraud policies.
